notes: The button straddles the breadboard centre gap in columns 4 and 6. Its top legs (side 1) are joined inside, as are its bottom legs (side 2).

The blue wire runs from Arduino pin 2 to column 6 of the top half, which is side 1 of the button. The black wire runs from GND to column 4 of the bottom half, which is side 2. Pressing the button connects D2 to GND.

The image labels the top half rows j-f and the bottom half rows e-a. The catalogue calls the top half bank 't' (rows a-e) and the bottom half bank 'b' (rows f-j). I followed the catalogue naming, so row letters are nominal. Only the column strip matters.
The sketch uses INPUT_PULLUP, so there is no external resistor. The circuit lists no LED.
The diagram shows the GND wire on the first GND pin in the power header, which I mapped to GND.1.
